summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis was admitted for acute-on-chronic pelvic pain characterized by sharp, intermittent left lower quadrant pain radiating to the rectum and left leg. Initial vitals showed tachycardia due to pain, which resolved with treatment. Physical exam revealed mild left lower quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs. A pelvic ultrasound showed a normal uterus and ovaries with no evidence of torsion or free fluid. Laboratory results, including WBC and lactate, were within acceptable limits, ruling out infection or ischemia. Pain was managed with intravenous and oral medications, including Dilaudid, gabapentin, ibuprofen, tramadol, and acetaminophen. The patient improved significantly, tolerated oral medications, and was discharged home on hospital day one with a stable condition. Follow-up was arranged with her gynecologist, and she was advised to monitor for warning signs including fever, severe pain, or abnormal bleeding.
